summary:
Item 'private' finished: the owner's own After Hours 07 values are out of the shipped tree (apart from old release notes, which the hard rules say not to touch). The anchor cases and the scene cases now find what they work on when they run instead of reading ids written into the code. Patch: 21 files, 479 lines added and 230 removed. It applies to a clean HEAD checkout (git apply --check). Nothing was committed. How the cases still run on the owner's backup: P01 is now written on Rail Demo. Its 'after_hours_07' entry gives no names, only how to find each one: its kind plus the words it says (sheet 'bench readings', 'rev a archived', 'rev b current'; calculation 'settled power', 'startup power'; rows of the Rev B sheet that say 'duration' and 'ceiling'). Before the first step, the scene case finds these names in the restored workspace with desk_scene.find_names. Each must be found exactly once, and two names must not resolve to the same thing; otherwise ValueError says which, in words. What the window reads is then said back in the scene's own names (desk_scene.said_back), so P01a..d are judged by exactly the same checks as DP01a..d. The anchors find their records with cases_anchor.found(): the reviewed sheet whose title says 'bench readings'; the standing calculations that read its B2 with B3 and with B4; the finding that carries settled power's result; and the PDF it was reviewed from, with its admitted SHA-256. Each must be found exactly once, or LookupError says which. records() now uses found() on Rail Demo too, so DA01/DA16/DA27 run the very code the anchors use on the backup, and they pass. Older commits still hold the values; git history was not rewritten.

numbers: Patch: 21 files, 479 lines added and 230 removed (git apply --stat on a clean HEAD archive; git apply --check passes)

Tests run on the throwaway copy: 51 modules in the default look and the 10 directly touched ones in the Kasandra look, all with 0 failures (counts in 'tests'); measured from each module's own 'Ran N tests' line
Fail-before check: the 14 tests of TheSceneOnAnotherWorkspace and TheCases, run against the old code with the new tests: 9 errors and 3 failures; all 14 pass after
Module times on this machine: test_rail_demo_campaign about 87 s, test_rail_demo about 121 s, test_desk_acts about 210 s, test_desk_scenes about 69 s (wall clock around each module)
Classification look: the backup zip holds 105 files; each owner value was found in 1 to 7 of them (counts only, private/look.py)
decisions: P01 is now written on Rail Demo, and the owner's workspace became the entry that finds its names (kind plus words), instead of the scene being written in the owner's names. Reason: no name of the owner's can stay in the file, while the scene still has to say some names.

The child says what the window read back in the scene's own names (said_back). P01a..d therefore keep the same expectations as DP01a..d, and the runner's parent, which never imports Graphite, needs no names. The case notes only WHICH names were found ('found'), not what they are called on the owner's backup. The step rows in a local result file still carry what the window read.
records() uses found() on both seeds, so the Rail Demo twins exercise the exact code that runs on the backup (DA01/DA16/DA27 pass with it).

No hash file beside the backup. The backup is identified by its shape: one sheet, two calculations, one finding and one admitted source must each be found exactly once. On top of that come the expected numbers, which are public, and the check that the sheet's source is the admitted PDF. docs/CAMPAIGN.md says this.
A16 no longer expects the sheet's title ('open_item'). A27 expects 'settled_results': ['3.6 W'] in place of the owner's calculation title. DA16 and DA27 still expect Rail Demo's titles.

The bench seed in test_desk_acts (played by test_desk_scenes as the scene is written) uses the scene's Rail Demo names, with Rail Demo's invented readings and limits imported as CSV. Constants READINGS, LIMITS_A, LIMITS_B were added there.
The name 'After Hours 07' and the seed name after_hours_07 are kept as the fixture's label: the zip is found by that name, and the task itself uses it.

In docs/MODEL_TRIAL_03.md the models' answers are kept, with each quoted name, text or size of the owner's replaced by a bracketed description and a note saying so, instead of deleting the trial record.
The gguf_fixture.py model file hash is left as it is: it is a published model's hash, not the owner's content.
No new test module, so tools/check_hatch.py FOCUSED_MODULES is unchanged.

desk_scene.find_names words the plural for rows as 'rows of <sheet>'. This message-only change was made after the broad runs; test_rail_demo_campaign (both looks) and test_desk_scenes were rerun on a fresh copy after it.
not_done: No case was run on the owner's After Hours 07 backup: the rule allowed looking at it only to classify. A01, A16, A17, A27 and P01a..d on the backup are not verified here. The owner or the coordinator can run: python3 tools/campaign.py run --case A01,A16,A17,A27,P01a,P01b,P01c,P01d --fixtures <folder holding Graphite_After_Hours_07.zip>. If the backup holds two things that match a search, or none, the case stops and names which one.

Release notes were not touched (hard rule). docs/RELEASE_NOTES_0.4.md, 0.4.2, 0.4.3, 0.5.0, 0.8.1 and 0.8.2 still quote the owner's titles, rows and numbers (for example '07 Bench readings', 'Pulse duration 120 ms to 80 ms', '110 ms less 80 ms'). The owner or the coordinator should decide on those.
Git history was not rewritten: older commits keep the ids, the hash and the names. wip/ (out of scope) also holds many copies.
project/stacy_seed/current and MANIFEST.json were not handed over; they regenerate. The seed's catalog.json still quotes the old DAILY_GUIDE example until then.
The 33 modules that import shell2, field_page, datasheet_work or kasandra_column (where only a comment or docstring changed) ran in the default look only.
Nothing ran on the owner's ThinkPad.
release_note: Graphite no longer carries anything from your own After Hours 07 workspace: no record ids, no file hash, no titles, and none of your readings. The playable scene is now written on Rail Demo, the invented workspace kept in the program. When your backup is present, the scene and the four anchor cases find what they need in it as they run, by what each thing is, and run as before. The numbers they expect there (12 V, 280 mA, 3.36 W, then 3.6 W) are the ones the first-run workshop already prints. Older commits still hold the earlier values; the history was not rewritten.
